summary: The v57 throne court summon diverges when consecutive hobgoblins are created: C redraws the next monster and suppresses its repeated appearance line with Norep(), while JavaScript routes that line through the ordinary message callback and adds a screen boundary. The owner is the runtime appearance tail of makemon.c:makemon and its Norep callback binding.

source.branch: Outside level generation, when MM_NOMSG is clear and the created monster has a discernible appearance, makemon redraws its square and calls Norep for the appearance line.
callers: sit.c:throne_sit_effect effect 7 calls makemon(courtmon(), tx, ty, NO_MM_FLAGS)

evidence: nethack-c/upstream/src/sit.c:112-123: throne_sit_effect effect 7 generates court monsters by calling makemon(courtmon(), tx, ty, NO_MM_FLAGS).
nethack-c/upstream/src/makemon.c:1468-1505: in runtime outside level generation, makemon calls newsym before formatting a visible appearance and sends that line through Norep().
nethack-c/upstream/src/pline.c:327-335: Norep sets PLINE_NOREPEAT before vpline, so repeated visible appearance text is suppressed while the square redraw still occurs.
js/sit.js:471-490: the effect-7 caller passes state, random, and its ordinary message callback to makemon_runtime without a distinct norepMessage callback.

js/makemon_create.js:2951-2961 and 3348-3363: the runtime appearance tail calls normalized.norepMessage, but makemon_runtime defaults that callback to the ordinary message callback whenever env.message is supplied; this bypasses ttyNorep's PLINE_NOREPEAT behavior.

The admitted v57 evaluation at challenges/evaluations/admission-01813882f5ec9612667f08b17e1630f732d78381-v57.json records 214/231 screens, 4039/4039 RNG calls, and 218/231 cursors; its first source mismatch is segment 0, input step 72, where the second identical hobgoblin appearance adds a boundary before the kobold redraw.
